claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi exposed to elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion will exhibit a lower wear rate than conventional stainless steel.
CoCrFeMnNi exposed to elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion will exhibit a lower corrosion current than conventional stainless steel.
Synergistic contributions from the constituent elements form a more stable and wear-resistant passive surface layer.
The proposed as-cast and homogenized CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a single-phase FCC structure.
Elevated-temperature sliding in a corrosive environment produces multicomponent surface oxides on CoCrFeMnNi.
Entropic stabilization of the alloying elements enables formation of a stable passive film.
Multiple principal elements in CoCrFeMnNi enhance passivation kinetics.
Solid-solution strengthening in CoCrFeMnNi reduces wear.
Enhanced passivation and solid-solution strengthening reduce simultaneous wear and corrosion rates at elevated temperatures.
CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit lower mass loss than 316 stainless steel under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit lower corrosion current density than 316 stainless steel under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
The proposed performance advantage applies when mechanical wear and corrosion occur concurrently at elevated temperature.
Changes in microstructure or corrosive medium may alter the outcome.
High-temperature tribo-corrosion data for this specific CoCrFeMnNi alloy are limited.
